units.passage: Describe how you will help them regulate their behavior and the temptation to use AI when it is not appropriate to do so. (For example, maybe students will have many low-stakes assessments, so they don’t need to feel anxious about their performance on any one assessment. Maybe they will do a lot of work in class with you or get support from peers, tutors, and you, so that they won’t need to be tempted to take shortcuts.
units.why: "Describe how you will help them regulate their behavior and the temptation to use AI when it is not appropriate" asks instructors to reduce the pressures behind misuse (e.g. "many low-stakes assessments"), which is P99.

units.passage: But you don’t need to use it anywhere else: you will get plenty of support during this course, so you don’t need to use AI inappropriately.
units.why: The sample statement says "you will get plenty of support during this course, so you don't need to use AI inappropriately", showing how to ease pressure by pointing to course support; P99 rather than P72 because it is about preventing misuse.
units.fit_note: Sample course policy text; also points to peers and instructor as human support.

units.passage: The good news is that there are multiple, research-based practices that can be used to minimize student cheating on essays and papers. In this guide, we describe eight such practices and provide brief examples of how to use them.
units.why: "research-based practices that can be used to minimize student cheating on essays and papers" sets the guide's approach as prevention by course design; P99 fits better than P36 since no sanction is described.
units.fit_note: Covers cheating in general (papers, ChatGPT), not AI only.

units.passage: And it is even more important that you then give students time to generate in writing their own ideas about how particular essay assignments will help them develop and learn. Optimally, this writing should happen in class and be saved in a Brightspace journal, so that students (or you) can return to these initial ideas as they complete or make progress on their writing assignment. It can be helpful to structure this reflection so that students make connections between the writing they’re doing and their academic and non-academic worlds. Students should share their ideas with each other and with you through a short in-class discussion.
units.why: Instructors give students time to write their own ideas on an assignment's value, saved in a Brightspace journal; this reduces the pressures leading to misuse, P99.

units.passage: As you design course activities that build toward the essay you want them to write, make sure that there are multiple opportunities for students to practice using the skills that assessment requires, and explicitly communicate the value of that practice to them.
units.why: "make sure that there are multiple opportunities for students to practice using the skills that assessment requires" aims to reduce anxiety that makes students "more likely to cheat", prevention of misuse pressure: P99.

units.passage: The best way to work against this feeling is to structure self-regulatory preparatory work right into your class.
units.why: "structure self-regulatory preparatory work right into your class" (planning for papers) is advice to reduce unpreparedness that drives cheating, P99.

units.passage: Help these students by having them analyze their efforts and the feedback you provide so they can be more successful.
units.why: "Help these students by having them analyze their efforts and the feedback you provide" targets the panic after a low grade that leads to cheating, a prevention step, P99.

units.passage: Other ways instructors can cultivate honesty include: spreadinglearners’ workload evenly throughout the course; requiring a description of process; reflecting on thepros/cons of AI; writing during class time; checking in with students throughout the term about what’sgoing well and what isn’t.
units.why: Ways to 'cultivate honesty include: spreading learners' workload evenly throughout the course; requiring a description of process', which eases pressures behind misuse (P99).
units.fit_note: Also lists process descriptions and in-class writing (P35).

units.passage: Making an effort to connect with your students can go a long way for creating community and a sense of connection, which is effective for combating cheating behaviors. Help your students see you as a human being who cares, is approachable, honest, and trustworthy. The good news is this - according to research, the sense of belonging you can create by connecting with students will not just help to create a class culture of integrity, but one of inclusivity as well.
units.why: "effective for combating cheating behaviors" is the stated reason for building belonging; connecting with students is a prevention measure, so P99.

units.passage: Provide students some choice and control over the assessments. For example, can the students choose their paper topic or even determine how much of their grade will come from assignments versus exams?
units.why: "Provide students some choice and control over the assessments" is advice to reduce the pressures behind cheating by giving choice, so P99.

units.passage: Provide multiple attempts at several low/ no-stakes assessments (formative) before the summative assessments
units.why: 'Provide multiple attempts at several low/no-stakes assessments' is an instructor action to ease grade pressure that drives cheating, so P99.

units.passage: After each assessment touchpoint, check in on your students' activities (CANVAS is helpful for this).
units.why: "check in on your students' activities" and Canvas engagement is a monitoring and outreach step to reduce temptation to use unpermitted aids, P99.

units.passage: Conducting Zoom conference calls with students who appear to be struggling (IAs can do this) and conducting at least one mid-quarter check with the entire class, not only shows that you care (which can reduce cheating) but it also may actually stop a student who would have been otherwise tempted to cheat.
units.why: "conducting at least one mid-quarter check with the entire class ... may actually stop a student who would have been otherwise tempted to cheat" is a prevention step, P99.

units.passage: Break larger assignments into smaller, scaffolded assignments to decrease the anxiety surrounding high-stakes assessments and to give you and your teaching team the opportunity to make early interventions if you suspect AI use.
units.why: "Break larger assignments into smaller, scaffolded assignments to decrease the anxiety surrounding high-stakes assessments" is justified by easing pressure and allowing early intervention, which fits P99 (reduce the pressures that lead to misuse); the assignment restructuring is secondary.
units.fit_note: A: Also gives the instructor chances for early intervention. B: Also aims to reduce anxiety (P99).

units.passage: Build in flexibility with guardrails to prevent students feeling “backed into a corner” by deadlines.
units.why: "Build in flexibility with guardrails to prevent students feeling “backed into a corner” by deadlines." recommends flexibility to reduce pressure, P99.

units.passage: While safeguarding the integrity of assessment practices is critical, it is equally important to recognize that cheating and plagiarism often stem from reasons other than lack of ethics.
units.why: "cheating and plagiarism often stem from reasons other than lack of ethics" names causes of misuse (unclear collaboration norms, overload from courses, jobs or family). P99 (reduce pressures that lead to misuse) is the closest type; the response itself (P68) is not stated.
units.fit_note: Gives reasons for misconduct rather than prescribing an educative response. / Names causes of misuse but does not itself prescribe extensions or support.

units.passage: There is a lot we can do, pedagogically, to scaffold assignments, make content accessible, and communicate the value and purpose of using generative AI critically and judiciously.
units.why: "There is a lot we can do, pedagogically, to scaffold assignments, make content accessible, and communicate the value and purpose of using generative AI critically and judiciously" urges instructors to ease the pressures behind misuse by scaffolding and explaining purpose. P99 for prevention; P66 is the second candidate, but scaffolding is the main action.

units.passage: This is also a great strategy to reduce the pressures students may feel with higher-stakes assessments, potentially reducing academic integrity concerns .
units.why: 'reduce the pressures students may feel with higher-stakes assessments, potentially reducing academic integrity concerns' is prevention by easing pressure (P99).

units.passage: This can help build intrinsic motivation and avoid the perception of assignments being mere exercises to achieve a grade.
units.why: Names building intrinsic motivation as a way to ease the grade pressure behind AI shortcuts: prevention (P99), informs.

units.passage: Providing specific guidelines in every assignment helps eliminate confusion and prevent unintentional academic misconduct. Resources to construct your syllabus statement: CLAS Syllabus template University of Iowa Center for Teaching and the Office of Teaching, Learning, and Technology Sentient Syllabus Project Syllabus Policies for Generative AI Tools
units.why: 'Providing specific guidelines in every assignment helps eliminate confusion and prevent unintentional academic misconduct' states the benefit of per-assignment rules (clarity prevents unintentional misuse), nearest P99.
units.fit_note: States that clear assignment-level guidelines prevent unintentional misconduct; the type covers reducing pressures behind misuse.

units.passage: Support academic integrity through transparent course and assignment expectations.
units.why: "Support academic integrity through transparent course and assignment expectations" ties integrity to clear per-assignment rules; P99 (prevention through clarity).

units.passage: it can create the conditions that make cheating feel like a viable option
units.why: Assessments disconnected from students' contexts "can create the conditions that make cheating feel like a viable option": reduce pressures that cause misuse, P99.
units.fit_note: Names assessment design as a cause of cheating.

units.passage: Additionally, creating assignments, policies, and grading schemes that reduce stress and enhance student motivation (and that address the root causes of academic dishonesty) will likely have a larger effect on students’ AI use than a simple syllabus policy.
units.why: "grading schemes that reduce stress and enhance student motivation (and that address the root causes of academic dishonesty)" recommends prevention by easing pressures; P99 rather than P35, which is about AI-proofing assessment.

units.passage: Please remember that some of the best practices in teaching and learning can help with mitigating the temptation to use AI.
units.policy: Best practices in teaching and learning, effective instruction and well-designed assessments can help reduce the temptation to use AI inappropriately.
units.why: 'effective instruction and well-designed assessments' reduce the 'temptation to use AI', so P99.

units.passage: Clear communication around the purpose of your assessments can help reduce student temptation to use AI inappropriately.
units.why: 'Clear communication around the purpose of your assessments can help reduce student temptation to use AI inappropriately' names prevention of misuse by explaining purpose, P99.

units.passage: making it particularly important to work on getting student buy-in for the learning process.
units.why: 'getting student buy-in for the learning process' is the page's answer to hard enforcement: win students over, P99.
units.fit_note: Aims to win student agreement rather than ease causes such as workload.

units.passage: Communicate with me and ask for help, even at the last minute, rather than risking your academic career
units.why: Required honesty language says dishonesty is 'driven by lack of time, desperation'; invites students to ask for help, easing pressure, P99.

units.passage: creating higher stakes for assignments creates an environment that can result in more cheating rather than less.
units.why: 'creating higher stakes for assignments creates an environment that can result in more cheating'; reducing pressure toward misuse, P99.

units.passage: Communicate with me and ask for help, even at the last minute, rather than risking your academic career
units.why: Statement invites students to 'Communicate with me and ask for help, even at the last minute'; easing pressure, P99.

units.passage: Effectively manage your time to complete assignments and reduce the risk of academic misconduct caused by last-minute pressure.
units.why: 'Effectively manage your time ... reduce the risk of academic misconduct caused by last-minute pressure'; easing pressure toward misuse, P99.

units.passage: If exams or quizzes are used, consider avoiding high-stakes weighting.
units.policy: If exams or quizzes are used, consider avoiding high-stakes weighting. Lower-stakes assessments can reduce pressure and discourage misuse while supporting skill development.
units.why: "If exams or quizzes are used, consider avoiding high-stakes weighting. Lower-stakes assessments can reduce pressure and discourage misuse" reduces the pressure that leads to misuse, so P99, instructor, before-course, should.

units.passage: Rather than simply relying on detection strategies, you may want to consider proactively addressing the use of generative AI and minimizing opportunities for the misuse of these tools.
units.why: "Rather than simply relying on detection strategies, you may want to consider proactively addressing the use of generative AI and minimizing opportunities for the misuse" recommends prevention over detection; P99 fits best, though it speaks of opportunities, not pressures.
units.fit_note: Concerns minimizing opportunities for misuse, not easing pressures. Also advises minimizing opportunities for misuse by assignment design, not only easing pressures.

units.passage: Students are more likely to exhibit academic dishonesty if they do not understand the purpose of a policy, are able to rationalize dishonest behavior or perceive that acting dishonestly is the norm among their peers.
units.why: "Students are more likely to exhibit academic dishonesty if they do not understand the purpose of a policy ... or perceive that acting dishonestly is the norm" gives causes of cheating as the basis for an integrity culture; P99, the causes of misuse.
units.fit_note: States causes of dishonesty as rationale for culture-building rather than prescribing a measure.

units.passage: Actions such as setting clear expectations, providing support and scaffolding to complete activities, appropriately challenging students, explaining the relevance of an activity and providing opportunities for growth can help motivate your students.
units.why: "setting clear expectations, providing support and scaffolding ... explaining the relevance of an activity and providing opportunities for growth" lists ways to motivate compliance by easing causes of misuse; P99.

units.passage: This reduces incentives to cheat and emphasizes student growth.
units.why: 'the more you can help students see why you have the assignments you do ... This reduces incentives to cheat and emphasizes student growth' ties explaining assignments to less cheating. P99 fits.

units.passage: Lang argues that cheating is not a problem with individual students, but it is rather a systemic issue where instructors are unintentionally creating learning environments that induce cheating.
units.why: 'cheating is not a problem with individual students, but it is rather a systemic issue where instructors are unintentionally creating learning environments that induce cheating' puts cheating pressure on course design. P99 fits.
units.fit_note: Argument from a cited book; ties to later redesign advice.

units.passage: Foster intrinsic motivation by allowing students to reflect on their own personal learning as much as possible.
units.why: 'Foster intrinsic motivation by allowing students to reflect on their own personal learning' is a way to reduce cheating pressure. P99 fits.

units.passage: Provide students numerous opportunities to demonstrate the learning they have
units.why: "Foster intrinsic motivation ... Emphasize mastery over performance ... Provide students numerous opportunities to demonstrate the learning" are course-structure changes to reduce cheating, P99.
units.fit_note: Also redesigns assessment toward lower-stakes, more frequent evidence (P35).

units.passage: Instill self-efficacy through metacognition by helping students hold themselves accountable for their own learning.
units.why: 'Instill self-efficacy through metacognition by helping students hold themselves accountable for their own learning' targets motivation. P99 fits.

units.passage: Academic pressure, time management difficulties, and stress can contribute to misconduct. Faculty are encouraged to remind students about available resources, such as:
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to remind students about available resources such as tutoring, writing assistance, office hours and counseling, because academic pressure, time management difficulties and stress can contribute to misconduct.
units.why: 'Academic pressure, time management difficulties, and stress can contribute to misconduct' and faculty should remind students of resources: prevention by easing pressures (P99).

units.passage: Instructors are encouraged to take a proactive approach to prevent misconduct using the teaching and communication strategies outlined above
units.why: 'Instructors are encouraged to take a proactive approach to prevent misconduct using the teaching and communication strategies' favors prevention through teaching (P99).
